The right move unlocks unified data, AI powered journeys, and sustainable growth. The wrong one creates disruption and sunk cost. This guide walks through the critical questions and evaluation steps so you can move with confidence and minimise risk. Summary A successful migration starts with a clear understanding of your current challenges and the capabilities you need from a new platform. From data readiness and AI capabilities to channels, customer journeys, implementation, and team readiness, this guide covers the key factors to evaluate before making a migration decision and how to measure its impact. Migration basics Assess your need for customer engagement platform migration Migration basics Assess your need for customer engagement platform migration Before comparing platforms, identify what is driving the migration and where your current platform falls short. Consider data accessibility, personalization, journey orchestration, channel coverage, analytics, integrations, and manual campaign management. Understanding these gaps helps you evaluate platforms against your actual business needs and avoid simply recreating existing limitations in a new system. Why Insider One Compare platforms Data readiness Audit your customer data before you switch platforms Data readiness Audit your customer data before you switch platforms A customer engagement platform is only as strong as the data behind it. Before migrating, map customer data across CRM, ecommerce, offline systems, and engagement tools. Assess data quality, identity resolution, and consent, and identify which sources should feed a unified customer database. With Insider One, you can centralize profiles and behavioral signals, then orchestrate journeys and personalization across supported channels from one foundation. Schedule a demo AI capabilities Evaluate AI, not just features and channels AI capabilities Evaluate AI, not just features and channels Modern migrations are driven by AI capabilities, not just feature parity. Compare how each platform uses AI to predict intent and churn, recommend content and products, and automate journeys. With Insider One, AI powers Agent One and Insider One AI, helping teams move from manual campaign building to autonomous, outcome-focused engagement that continuously optimizes conversion and customer lifetime value. Explore Insider One AI Journey orchestration Plan and optimize your customer journeys Journey orchestration Plan and optimize your customer journeys Migration is not a copy-paste exercise. Use it to rethink journeys like onboarding, replenishment, cart recovery, and winback. Decide which journeys to replicate, retire, or replace with AI-driven orchestration. Insider One lets you rebuild journeys visually across supported channels and use predictive segments like “new customers” and “cannot lose them” to target high-value audiences. Explore journey orchestration Evaluation criteria Key questions to answer before you migrate Use these questions as a structured checklist when assessing any customer engagement platform against your current stack. Does it unify all your customer data Confirm that the platform can ingest behavioural, transactional, and CRM data from online and offline sources into a single customer profile. Ask how identity resolution works, how quickly data becomes actionable, and whether AI models use this unified view to power segments and journeys in real time. Can it orchestrate journeys across every priority channel Map your critical channels, including web, app, email, SMS, WhatsApp, site search, and web push. Check that the platform natively supports these touchpoints and lets you build cross channel journeys without custom engineering. Insider One provides orchestration across its web, app, messaging, and on site products from one interface. How mature are its AI agents and assistants Look beyond buzzwords. Review how the platform’s AI agents behave in production, whether they can autonomously recommend actions, and how they integrate with your data. With Agent One and Insider One AI, you get purpose built agents for shopping, support, and insights that operate on your own customer profiles. What is the implementation and migration model Migration cost and complexity vary massively between vendors. Ask who handles data mapping, channel setup, and testing, how long it takes to go live, and what happens if expectations are not met. Insider One’s $0 Migration Movement includes white glove implementation in your platform fee. Migration planning workshop Design your migration roadmap with Insider One If you are considering a move from your current customer engagement platform, a structured migration plan reduces risk and speeds up time to value. Work with Insider One’s team to assess data, channels, and AI requirements, then define a phased rollout that aligns with your goals and resources. Book a consultation Explore $0 Migration Movement Comparing vendors How to compare Insider One with your current platform When evaluating a migration, buyers often compare Insider One with Adobe, Salesforce, Braze, Bloomreach, Iterable, Klaviyo, CleverTap, and MoEngage. Focus on these practical differences. Unified platform versus stitched tools Many vendors offer separate products for data, personalization, and messaging that require custom integration. Insider One brings customer data management, personalization, journey orchestration, and analytics together in one platform so your team can operate from a single source of truth. Native AI agents and assistants Some platforms bolt AI onto existing workflows. Insider One embeds AI throughout the product, from predictive segments and recommendations to Agent One’s autonomous agents and Insider One AI’s analytics assistant. This lets you shift from manual configuration to AI driven decision making. Breadth of natively supported channels Channel gaps add complexity and cost. Compare which channels require third party tools. Insider One natively supports web, app, email, SMS, WhatsApp, web push, and site search, so cross channel journeys and personalization happen inside one system without extra connectors. Migration cost and risk Implementation fees and long contracts increase risk if the platform under delivers. Insider One’s $0 Migration Movement includes white glove onboarding in your platform fee and offers an opt out with a full refund in the first months if expectations are not met. Reduce migration risk with the $0 Migration Movement Cost and risk are two major migration blockers. Explore the $0 Migration Movement Operational readiness Prepare your team for migration Technology migration succeeds only when teams are ready. These factors help you plan internal readiness. Skills and ownership Identify who will own customer engagement post migration, from CRM and marketing to data and product teams. Assess skills in journey design, experimentation, and AI usage. Insider One’s interface and academy content are designed to support marketers and CRM teams, not only engineers. Governance and compliance Confirm how consent, preferences, and regional regulations will be handled in the new platform. Document governance for data usage, segmentation, and AI decisions so teams know what is allowed and why. Use Insider One’s unified data foundation to keep profiles and permissions consistent across channels. Testing and experimentation Plan how you will validate that migrated journeys perform better than the old setup. Establish a testing framework for personalization, messaging, and journey logic. Insider One’s analytics and reporting help you measure uplift, diagnose bottlenecks, and iterate quickly. Rollout phases and change management Avoid a big bang switch. Define phased rollouts by country, brand, or channel, and communicate clearly with stakeholders so they understand new workflows and outcomes. Use pilot groups to prove value early and build confidence before full migration. If you are layering point solutions or relying heavily on custom workarounds, evaluating a unified platform like Insider One can reduce complexity and unlock growth. How long does it typically take to migrate to a new customer engagement platform Timelines vary by data complexity, number of channels, and internal resources. A structured migration usually runs in phases, starting with core data and priority journeys, then expanding to additional channels and use cases. Insider One’s $0 Migration Movement includes white glove implementation to accelerate setup and minimise disruption. What risks should I consider before switching platforms Common risks include data loss, journey downtime, limited feature parity, and underestimating internal change management. Mitigate them by auditing data, documenting current journeys, planning rollback options, and choosing a vendor that offers strong implementation support and clear performance guarantees, such as Insider One’s refund promise. How do I compare Insider One to vendors like Adobe, Salesforce, Braze, Bloomreach, Iterable, Klaviyo, CleverTap, or MoEngage Focus on unified data, AI maturity, channel coverage, and migration terms. Compare whether each vendor offers a single platform for data, personalization, and journeys, how AI agents operate in practice, which channels are natively supported, and what implementation and refund policies look like. Insider One is designed to consolidate these capabilities. Do I need a dedicated data team to migrate to Insider One A data team helps with complex integrations, but it is not mandatory. Many brands migrate with marketing and CRM teams working alongside Insider One’s implementation specialists. The goal is to connect your key data sources, validate identity and consent, and ensure that marketers can use unified profiles and AI powered tools in their daily workflows. Legal information. Accept All Only Necessary Decline All Manage consent Close Privacy Overview This website uses cookies to improve your experience while you navigate through the website. Out of these cookies, the cookies that are categorized as necessary are stored on your browser as they are essential for the working of basic functionalities of the website. We also use third-party cookies that help us analyze and understand how you use this website. These cookies will be stored in your browser only with your consent. You also have the option to opt-out of these cookies. But opting out of some of these cookies may have an effect on your browsing experience. Necessary Necessary Always Enabled Necessary cookies are absolutely essential for the website to function properly. These cookies ensure basic functionalities and security features of the website, anonymously. The cookie is used to calculate visitor, session, campaign data and keep track of site usage for the site's analytics report.
